title: Solving Britain's energy bottlenecks: The £78 billion-a-year opportunity for cleaner, more affordable power
figure_ref: Article paragraph on UK transmission constraint costs, citing National Audit Office, Sep 11 2026 (not source six-value-pool exhibit)
business_context: McKinsey frames six bottleneck-related UK energy value pools totaling about £78bn annual commercial opportunity in 2030. It separately cites the National Audit Office's observation of £1.9bn transmission constraint costs in 2025/26. Absent coordinated grid action the cited outlook could reach £7.8bn per year by 2030.
key_message: Without concerted upgrades, annual UK transmission constraint costs could rise from £1.9 billion in FY2025/26 to £7.8 billion by 2030, a conditional £5.9 billion increase.
so_what: Prioritize transmission-grid bottlenecks by potential annual system cost, while keeping conditional outcomes separate from committed spending.
original_chart_type: Six energy value-pool exhibit (SVG, inaccessible to graphic comparison)
encoding: x=period/status, y=annual GBP billions, fill+hatching=observed versus conditional forecast, direct labels and computed £5.9bn difference.

data_recipe: Define annual network constraint costs as the comparable metric.

message_conditions: The £7.8bn estimate is conditional on insufficient grid upgrades.
Each number is an annual amount, not a cumulative multi-year amount.
Inflation basis for the National Audit Office constraint-cost comparison is not stated in this article.
